{{Short description|Israeli mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=January 2021}}
'''Itay Neeman''' ({{Langx|he|איתי נאמן}}; born 1972) is an Israeli [[set theory|set theorist]] working as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/people/ladder/ineeman|title=Itay Neeman|work=Faculty|publisher=UCLA Mathematics|accessdate=2021-01-29}}</ref> He has made  major contributions to the theory of [[inner model]]s, [[determinacy]] and [[Forcing (mathematics)|forcing]].<ref name=hausdorff/>

==Early life and education==
Neeman was born in 1972 in [[Safed]], [[Israel]]. After studying mathematics at [[King's College London]] and the [[University of Oxford]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.wiko-berlin.de/en/fellows/academic-year/2005/neeman-itay|title=Itay Neeman, Ph.D.|year=2005|work=Fellows|publisher=[[Berlin Institute for Advanced Study]]|accessdate=2021-01-29}}</ref> he earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]]  at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1996, under the supervision of [[John R. Steel]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=22129}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Neeman won a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|CAREER Award]] in 2001.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200201/people.pdf|title=2001 CAREER Awards Made|department=Mathematics People|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|page=42|volume=49|issue=1|date=January 2002}}</ref> He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2006.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=neeman|title=Neeman, Itay|work=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|publisher=International Mathematical Union|accessdate=2021-01-30}}</ref> In 2012, the [[Simons Foundation]] named Neeman as one of their Simons Fellows, in the inaugural year of the Simons Fellows program.<ref>{{citation|url=http://homepage.math.uiowa.edu/~whan/SimonsFellow1.pdf|title=Simons Foundation|newspaper=New York Times|date=March 6, 2012|type=Paid advertisement congratulating Simons Fellows}}</ref>

In 2019 he was awarded the [[Hausdorff Medal]], by the European Set Theory Society. The award cited three of his papers for their work on "iterating forcing using side conditions and the tree property" as having been the most significant contribution to set theory in the previous five years.<ref name=hausdorff>{{citation|url=https://sites.google.com/view/estc2019/estc-2019/the-hausdorff-medal|title=The Hausdorff Medal|work=European Set Theory Conference 2019|publisher=European Set Theory Society|accessdate=2021-01-29}}</ref>
